must_identify.text: The detections are presented as one chain on corpws63 (198.51.100.63): cmd.exe starts C:\Users\Public\Libraries\svchost.exe under u-fin22, that process connects to internal hosts on 445/tcp and 3389/tcp, and the network sensor's two Suricata sweep alerts from the same address follow within two minutes.

The svchost.exe in C:\Users\Public\Libraries is identified as masquerading (T1036.005): a Windows binary name running outside System32, started by cmd.exe under a user account at Medium integrity rather than by the service control manager.
The fan-out to 445/tcp and 3389/tcp across many internal 198.51.100.x hosts is identified as network service discovery (T1046), the kind of sweep that precedes lateral movement over SMB or RDP.

The brief compares the sweep with the recon delta and concludes it is not the scheduled recon run: different source host (corpws63, not corpscan11), different address (198.51.100.63, not 192.0.2.11) and different time (15:42Z to 15:44Z on 2026-08-17, not 02:00Z to 02:41Z on 2026-08-18).

Data requests or options cover the binary itself (its hash or a copy), what started the parent cmd.exe, and whether any swept host accepted an SMB or RDP session from 198.51.100.63 (logons on the targets or flow records); options include isolating corpws63.

must_not.text: The sweep is not dismissed or downgraded as the scheduled recon scan, as authorized scanning, or as an expected inventory job.
The svchost.exe process is not treated as the legitimate Windows service host.
